subject: Custom SLA addendum request — availability boundary & order form exhibit
messages:
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
From: Emily Torres <emily.torres@cardiohealth.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Contracts Team <contracts@cardiohealth.ai>
Subject: Request: tailored availability exhibit & order form language

Hi Ben —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. CardioHealth is excited about Redwood’s throughput and the regional failover patterns you showed. Legal/procurement has one ask before we proceed: we need a formal SLA addendum (exhibit) and suggested order form language that (a) captures a 99.95% monthly availability commitment for our primary region, (b) defines latency guardrails for LLM inference p99 for short prompt paths, and (c) documents the exception carveouts for scheduled maintenance and force majeure.

Two specific asks:
- Can you provide wording that slots into our master services agreement (MSA) as an electronic exhibit (MSA Exhibit A)?
- We’d like an order form paragraph (short snippet) that procurement can paste into a one-page order form for signature.

We can share our standard MSA if helpful — I attached a short data map and our procurement checklist.

Attached: CHAI_Cardio_data_map_v1.pdf

Best,
Emily Torres
Head of Procurement
CardioHealth AI

Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Emily Torres <emily.torres@cardiohealth.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Subject: Re: Request: tailored availability exhibit & order form language

Emily —

Appreciate the note and the data map. We can absolutely put together an SLA exhibit and a short order-form snippet. Kimberley from our legal/solutions team (cc’d) will propose MSA exhibit language and Marissa will surface operational evidence paths for availability/latency.

Quick timeline proposal:
- Today: we’ll draft a focused exhibit (1–2 pages) and a one-paragraph order form snippet.
- Tomorrow: Kimberley will send redlines and a proposed evidence/resolution flow (what telemetry we provide, runbook references, and service-credit schedule).

Two clarifying questions for CardioHealth to help scope carveouts:
1) For scheduled maintenance, do you require a minimum advance notice (we typically do 48–72 hours for non-critical updates)?
2) For latency p99 you referenced, are you looking for an absolute ms target for a 32-token or 64-token prompt (helps us pick the right model profile and kernel path)?

I’m attaching our initial draft exhibit and a working document where Kimberley can add redlines.

Attachments: draft_sla_exhibit_benc_v1.docx

—
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0139

Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 14:27:00 -07:00
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Emily Torres <emily.torres@cardiohealth.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Subject: Re: Request: tailored availability exhibit & order form language

Emily / Ben —

I pulled the draft and added targeted redlines focusing on: definition clarity (what counts as "availability" vs "degraded mode"), an explicit schedule for notification of scheduled maintenance (we propose 72 hours for regular maintenance; emergency maintenance defined separately), and a concise service-credit table tied to monthly uptime percentage.

A few notes / asks from legal:
- We prefer carving out latency from the main uptime metric and express it as a separate operational target (p99 inference latency for 32-token baseline: 250ms). If CardioHealth wants a stricter p99 target, that will map to a different model profile and Dedicated capacity options (cost implication).
- For exception handling when a customer requests custom quantization/third-party plugin integration, we need that to be scoped as a non-standard configuration that may affect availability commitments — would you accept language that flags such integrations as "deployment-specific exceptions"?
- Please confirm whether DocuSign or our standard signature block is preferred for countersigning the exhibit.

I attached my redlines as a tracked document — Ben, can you forward the file to Emily and the contracts team?

Attachments: redlines_benc_kpark_v1.docx

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Commercial
Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com

Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 16:03:00 -07:00
From: Emily Torres <emily.torres@cardiohealth.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Contracts Team <contracts@cardiohealth.ai>
Subject: Re: Request: tailored availability exhibit & order form language

Kim / Ben —

Thanks for the fast turnaround and the redlines. The CardioHealth procurement team is generally supportive of the structure you proposed. A couple of confirmations and one request:

1) Scheduled maintenance notice: 72 hours is acceptable.
2) Latency target: we’d like to start with the 32-token p99 @ 250ms as you suggested, and we’ll evaluate Dedicated capacity if we see variance during pilot.
3) Deployment-specific exceptions: acceptable, but we require a short clause that requires prior written consent from CardioHealth before Redwood applies any third-party runtime that could materially affect availability.

We are ready to move forward — Contracts team will prepare the MSA countersign flow. Please route the redlined exhibit to our contracts alias and we’ll start internal approvals. For signatures, DocuSign link is preferred.

DocuSign (provisional): https://www.docusign.com/en/link/CHAI-SLA-EXHIBIT-8420

Emily Torres
Head of Procurement
CardioHealth AI
